info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
info.description:
At the end of this course, students will be able to:
1.Background Knowledge: (ABET e)
- Understand the role and functions of an operating system.
- Grasp important OS concepts such as kernels, file systems, and process management.
- Comprehend the mechanisms of operating systems, including memory hierarchy and CPU roles.
- Identify and analyze main problems and challenges in operating systems.
2.Practical Skills: (ABET k)
- Use basic and advanced shell commands in a Linux system fluently.
- Develop proficiency in shell scripting on Linux.
- Address and solve key operating system problems through practical exercises and simulations.
3.Information Searching, Reading, and Selection Skills: (ABET i)
- Efficiently search for, read, and select relevant information related to operating systems and Linux.
4.Teamwork, Documentation, and Presentation Skills: (ABET g)
- Work effectively in groups to complete projects.
- Document and present findings and solutions clearly and professionally.
info.studentTasks:
- Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination.
- Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time
- Use laptop in class only for learning purpose
- Promptly access to the FU LMS https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
info.tools:
- Internet
- Linux (CentOS, Ubuntu) operating system server and/or client

materials.author: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter Baer Galvin, Greg Gagne

clos.loDetails: Grasp the core concepts of operating systems, including the kernel, process management, memory management, and file systems.
Understand how operating systems manage resources within the context of Linux.
Utilize the command line to operate and administer the Linux system.
Master regular expressions and shell scripting to automate tasks and manage system operations.
Develop advanced practical skills in Linux system administration.
Learn and implement basic security solutions on Linux systems.
Configure and understand TCP/IP networking protocols.
Set up and manage services on Linux systems.
Use AI, standard tools and techniques to manage, maintain, and troubleshoot Linux systems.
